name: BEN Drowned
description: A multimedia online horror narrative and alternate reality game by Alexander D. Hall ('Jadusable') begun on 4chan's /x/ board on 7 September 2010, framed as a haunted Nintendo 64 cartridge of The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask possessed by an entity called BEN.
full_description: BEN Drowned is a foundational creepypasta and alternate reality game (ARG) created by American writer Alexander D. Hall (online handle 'Jadusable'). It originally appeared as a thread titled 'Haunted Majora's Mask Cartridge' on 4chan's paranormal /x/ board on 7 September 2010, and unfolded as a daily multimedia serial through 15 September 2010. The story-within-the-story is told by 'Jadusable', a college sophomore who acquires a used Nintendo 64 cartridge of The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask (Nintendo, 2000) from an old man at a yard sale. The cartridge contains a save file named 'BEN'; subsequent gameplay sessions are recorded as YouTube videos showing increasingly glitched and uncanny behavior — Link being burned by the Happy Mask Salesman, the Elegy of Emptiness statue stalking the player, and the file repeatedly resetting itself. Through the in-fiction Cleverbot conversations and YouTube videos, an entity claims to be BEN, identified with a child who drowned. The narrative evolved into a multi-year ARG ('Moon Children', 'Arc 2: The Truth', etc.) and is widely considered one of the most influential works in the creepypasta genre, helping establish creepypasta as a recognized literary form. The series ran intermittently from 2010 to 2020.
origin: Internet-native phenomenon; primarily distributed via 4chan's /x/ board, YouTube, and Jadusable's hosted website. Audience is global English-speaking internet users.

etymology.origin: Coined by Alexander D. Hall in his 7 September 2010 4chan /x/ post; 'BEN' is the name of the save file on the haunted cartridge, and 'Drowned' is added because the in-fiction backstory (delivered through the haunted gameplay and Cleverbot dialogue) suggests BEN is the spirit of a boy who drowned.
etymology.meaning: Literal: a (fictional) boy named Ben who drowned, whose spirit haunts a Nintendo 64 cartridge.
etymology.first_use: 2010-09-07: 'Haunted Majora's Mask Cartridge' thread on 4chan's /x/ board (Alex Hall / Jadusable)
